messages:
Maya Patel: FYI customer AcmeAnalytics just opened an escalation — they're seeing intermittent 5xx / 504s from the hosted API over the last 45m. P95 shot up and a few tail timeouts. ticket #INC-2134. attaching a snippet of the customer's timeline they sent.

Jordan (support): timeline says errors started after a large nightly batch. They saw repeated 502/504 and a lot of client retries. No config changes on their side reported.

Omar Reyes: can you paste the original request ids so we can correlate to gateway logs?

Jordan (support): sending two sample request_ids: req_20260315_01 and req_20260315_07. Also the customer noticed auth refreshes failing around the same time (401 -> retry loop).

SRE-bot: automated alert: hosted-gateway p99 latency > 7s for 15m (metric: gateway.request.latency.percentile).

Lucy (sre): grabbing queue metrics now. Running `curl -s http://metrics.internal/hosted/queues | jq '.continuous_batcher'` gave: ```{"queue_depth": 748, "queue_limit": 800, "p95_ms": 3200, "p99_ms": 8900, "inflight": 96}```

Ryan (eng-runtime): 748/800 is dangerously close. That explains the tail spikes — continuous batcher backlog hitting depth cap and forcing early rejects/timeouts. Any recent deploys?

Ben (oncall_lead): we rolled a small runtime tweak 1h ago (hash fb2c3). It included a change to kv-cache eviction timing. Could that change increase memory pressure -> slow KV lookups and hold batch slots longer?

Ryan (eng-runtime): possible. The change reduced aggressive eviction which can keep larger KV cache. If cache misses are more expensive on the new kernel, per-request latency could increase and queue drains slower. I'm looking at the canary logs now.

Lucy (sre): also seeing increased 401 spikes in auth gateway: `auth.refresh.errors 45/m` during the window. Those 401-caused client retries likely increased request fanout.

Maya Patel: customer reports that when errors appear, their client retries quickly (no jitter). They use short retry backoff which probably amplified stacked requests.

Jordan (support): customer asked if this could be billing/rate-limit related — they saw some 429s earlier in the morning but most of the current 5xx are 504/gateway timeouts.

Omar Reyes: pulled gateway logs for req_20260315_01: ```[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] req_20260315_01 tenant=acme status=504 backend=continuous-batcher queue_depth=762 exec_ms=8123```. Multiple entries show long exec_ms before timing out.

Ryan (eng-runtime): exec_ms ~8s lines up with p99. That means requests are queuing for multiple seconds waiting for batch slot. If queue_depth > queue_limit we start rejecting or timing out. Our continuous-batching backlog policy uses queue_limit=800 and max_wait_ms=8000 currently.

Ben (oncall_lead): immediate mitigation options? Increase queue_limit? Enable overflow fallback to non-batched path? Temporarily scale more batchers?

Lucy (sre): we can temporarily increase queue_limit to 1024 and spin up +2 batcher pods on hosted pool. Risk: more memory usage, might hide root cause but buys time for customer.

Ryan (eng-runtime): also we have a fallback route to smaller model variant (less token length) which avoids the heavy KV ops. We could route AcmeAnalytics to the smaller variant for the next 2 hours. That should reduce per-request exec_ms.

Maya Patel: customer asked for a repro — they want steps we took so they can test. Jordan can we give them a minimal repro script?

Jordan (support): suggested repro steps to customer: 1) send burst of concurrent requests with short retry backoff (no jitter) 2) include long sequences (2000 tokens) to hit KV heavy path 3) observe intermittent 504s when queue saturates. Provided curl snippet.

Jordan (support): ```bash
for i in {1..400}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"xlarge-embed","input":"<big prompt>"}' &
done; wait
```

Omar Reyes: also dumped batcher logs: ```[2026-03-15T09:11:35Z] batcher:allocating batch id=234 size=64 wait_ms=5400 kv_hits=0 kv_misses=64```. High kv_misses suggests cache miss storm.

Ryan (eng-runtime): kv_misses x64 per batch is bad. Looks like a cache eviction policy change did cause higher miss rate under these keys. I'll roll back the fb2c3 canary immediately for hosted.

Ben (oncall_lead): action plan enacted: 1) Lucy increased queue_limit -> 1024 (temporary) 2) spun up +2 batcher pods 3) routed acme tenant to smaller model variant 4) Ryan rolling back fb2c3 canary.

SRE-bot: deploy event: rollback fb2c3 -> success at 2026-03-15T09:25:02Z.

Lucy (sre): after mitigation metrics: `queue_depth` dropped from ~760 -> 210 in 6m, p99 dropped from 8.9s -> 1.2s. Customer reported reduced errors.

Jordan (support): passed mitigations to AcmeAnalytics; they're running the repro workload now and report far fewer timeouts. They're happy with temporary workaround, asking for root cause explanation and long-term fix.

Maya Patel: root cause summary draft: continuous-batcher backlog due to combined factors: 1) auth refresh errors causing retry amplification 2) runtime kv-cache policy change increased cache misses and per-request exec time 3) customer retry behavior with low jitter increased pressure. Temp mitigations applied.

Ryan (eng-runtime): long-term fixes proposed: revert kv-cache change permanently or rework eviction to be workload-aware; add jittered client-retry guidance in our docs; implement automatic overflow fallback to non-batched path before hitting queue_limit; and add per-tenant admission control to prevent single tenant from saturating batchers.

Ben (oncall_lead): I'll open a follow-up engineering ticket ENG-8904 for eviction policy and ENG-8905 for overflow fallback. Jordan, please keep INC-2134 updated with rollback and metrics.

Jordan (support): will do. Closing the customer-facing loop now.

Maya Patel: thanks team — keep monitoring for 2 hours and if metrics regress we escalate to priority. :thumbsup:
